method: PRODUCED - CONSUMED symbol parity (rg across src/, src/bin/, interfaces/, shared/), read-before-write triage

findings.produced: MediaPolicy struct with 6 pub serde fields (max_image_bytes/max_audio_bytes/max_video_duration/max_video_bytes/max_document_bytes/max_document_pages), 6 serde default fns, Default impl, JsonSchema, re-exported at lib.rs:232
findings.consumer_location: none found outside policy.rs tests and pipeline.rs:26 (MediaPolicy::default()); rg -n "MediaPolicy" src/ src/bin/ interfaces/ shared/ returned only lib.rs:232 re-export, policy.rs tests, pipeline.rs:4/17/26, mod.rs docs; rg on the six field names outside policy.rs returned nothing
findings.rationale: check_size (policy.rs:71) is production-reachable via pipeline.rs:60 (FilePath inputs from the three media tools), but the configuration surface is severed: MediaPipeline::new() hardcodes MediaPolicy::default() (pipeline.rs:26) and has no setter, no config loader references the field names, and no code reads them. serde/JsonSchema promise a config story with zero producers/consumers (form 6 orphaned pub API + form 5 drift). Public lib API (lib.rs re-export) so CUT has external-compat risk; needs human judgment.
findings.proposed_change: Option A (CUT surface): make fields private, drop serde/JsonSchema/default fns, keep in-memory defaults and check_size. Option B (CONNECT): add a [media] config section + MediaPipeline::with_policy setter and read it in agent_init/constructor. Option C: leave as-is, documented as default-only.
findings.risk: low for option A: no in-repo reader of fields or serde form; MediaPolicy is not in any exported schema (export_desktop_bridge_schema covers aleph_protocol, not alephcore). External alephcore consumers (shells/plugins) are the only breakage surface.
findings.verification: rg -n "MediaPolicy" src/ src/bin/ interfaces/ shared/ (evidence above); rg -n "max_video_duration|max_image_bytes|max_audio_bytes|max_video_bytes|max_document_bytes|max_document_pages" src/ src/bin/ interfaces/ shared/ --glob '!src/media/policy.rs' -> no output. After change: rg for the field names returns only policy.rs.

findings.produced: VideoFormat enum (Mp4/WebM/Mov) and MediaType::Video, produced by detect_video_extension (detect.rs:56-58), detect_ftyp_magic (detect.rs:180-208), detect_video_magic (detect.rs:210-217)
findings.consumer_location: no production reader of the VideoFormat value; sole production reader of MediaType::Video is policy.rs:97 (size/duration branch, format unread); rg -n "VideoFormat" src/ src/bin/ interfaces/ shared/ shows construction only (detect.rs) plus tests (detect.rs:337/344/351/457, policy.rs:202/212, types.rs:152); rg -n "MediaType::Video" src/ | rg -v test shows detect.rs construction + policy.rs:97 only
findings.rationale: Video detection feeds the media_understand tool, whose DESCRIPTION (understand.rs:84) advertises 'images, audio, video, documents', but the pipeline's only registered providers are image/document/audio (constructor/mod.rs:380-390). Every video media_understand call fails with MediaError::NoProvider { media_type: "video" }. VideoFormat is produced-but-never-read dead data (form 1); the tool's video claim is name-drift (form 5). Whether to wire a video provider or cut video support is a product judgment, so DECIDE.
findings.proposed_change: Option A (CONNECT): add a video provider (frame extraction into the existing VisionPipeline/ImageMediaProvider). Option B (CUT): drop video detection (detect_video_extension, ftyp video branch, detect_video_magic, VideoFormat, MediaType::Video) and scrub 'video' from understand.rs:84. Option C: leave as forward-looking scaffolding.
findings.risk: Option A additive. Option B changes detect_by_extension("mp4") from Ok(Video) to Err(UnsupportedFormat); the tool already maps that to a readable error and nothing matches on VideoFormat's data, so risk is low. Policy video branch (policy.rs:97-117) would become unreachable if CUT.
findings.verification: rg -n "VideoFormat" src/ src/bin/ interfaces/ shared/ (construction+tests only); rg -n "MediaType::Video" src/ | rg -v test (detect construction + policy.rs:97). After fix: video media_understand either succeeds (CONNECT) or yields UnsupportedFormat (CUT).
